You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

This looks like a task where shapes (hollow rectangles) need to be... moved? Common ARC task: smaller objects (5, 6 boxes) are scaled-up versions contained inside larger... Actually there's one big 9 rectangle (8x8 hollow) and smaller 5 (3x4 hollow) and 6 (5x5 hollow). Typical rule: the largest rectangle stays, smaller ones... Actually task might be "extend/copy": smaller shapes are scaled versions to fill? Or perhaps the 5 and 6 shapes grow to match the 9 shape? Or they shrink? Need demos. This is ambiguous; request a demo.

Rule: fill interiors of hollow rectangles with a color. In demo, interior filled with 7 — but the 3-box interior got filled with 2, and 5-box interior got 7. Hmm: 5's interior became 7, 1's interiors 7, 3's interior 2, 5's interior 7. So color varies: larger interiors = 7, smaller (2x2) = 2? Interior sizes: 5-rect interior 3x3 → 7; 1-rect interior 3x5 → 7; 3-rect interior 2x2 → 2; 5-rect interior 1x1 → 7?? 1x1 filled with 7 but 2x2 filled with 2. Hmm.

Maybe color by rectangle size: total area? Or perimeter? Interiors with area ≥? 1x1→7, 3x3→7, 3x5→7, 2x2→2. Weird. Maybe color relates to rectangle dimensions: heights×widths: 5x5, 7x7, 7x9, 4x4, 3x3. Small ones (3x3 →7?) vs 4x4→2? Not consistent.

Maybe color = something like count of rectangles? Or color determined by parity? Dimensions: 5's: h5w5→7; 1's: h7w7→7; 3's: h4w4→2; last 5's: h3w3→7. Odd heights→7, even→2? 5 odd→7, 7 odd→7, 4 even→2, 3 odd→7. Yes! Parity of height (or both dims same parity since squares here). But test rectangles aren't squares.

Test: 9-rect 7x7 interior 5x5? Rect at rows1-7, cols0-7: h7,w8. Second 9-rect rows4-11, cols20-27: h8,w8. 5-rect rows11-14 cols1-4: h4,w4. 6-rect rows12-16 cols12-16: h5,w5.

Fill color rule by parity... in demo all rects: 5x5(odd,odd)→7; 7x7→7; 4x4(even)→2; 3x3→7. Maybe rule: interior area? interior areas: 9,25,15,1,4. Maybe fill with number of... Hmm 1x1 interior got 7 and 2x2 got 2.

Maybe the fill color = color of rectangle scaled? Alternatively maybe fill color depends on whether width and height have same parity? 4x4 both even → 2; 3x3 both odd → 7; 5x5 →7; 7x7→7. Test rects: 7x8 mixed; 8x8 even→2?; 4x4→2; 5x5→7. Hmm that leaves mixed 7x8 ambiguous.

Alternative: fill color = number of rectangles? demo has 4 rects, fills 7 and 2. Maybe fill color = interior dimension sum mod something? interior dims: 3x3→7? 1x1→7, 3x5→7, 2x2→2. Maybe fill = max(3,...)? Perhaps fill color = interior height+width? 3+3=6 no.

Maybe fill color depends on grid position? Rects filled with 7 are in left column/top... positions: 5-rect top-left→7; 1-rect top-right→7; 1-rect bottom-left→7; 3-rect right-middle→2; 5-rect bottom-middle→7. Not positional.

Maybe fill color = 7 for larger rectangles, 2 for smaller, and 1x1 exception... 1x1 interior got 7 though. Hmm wait check last 5-rect: rows24-26, cols10-12, output rows25: "5 7 5" — interior single cell =7. So 1x1→7, 2x2→2, 3x3→7, 3x5→7. So maybe fill color = parity: odd dimension(s) →7, even →2? 1x1 odd→7 ✓, 2x2 even→2 ✓, 3x3 odd→7 ✓, 3x5 odd→7 ✓. Rule: fill interior with 7 if interior height is odd else 2? All interior dims odd→7, even→2 consistently (both dims same parity here).

Test interiors:
- 9-rect1: rows1-7 cols0-7, interior rows2-6 cols1-6: 5x5 odd → 7.
- 9-rect2: rows4-11 cols20-27, interior rows5-10 cols21-26: 6x6 even → 2.
- 5-rect: interior 2x2 → 2.
- 6-rect: rows12-16 cols12-16, interior rows13-15 cols13-15: 3x3 odd → 7.

But parity of which dim? They agree in demo. For test, all interiors have equal-parity dims except 5x5 (odd) fine, 6x6 even, 2x2, 3x3. Good.

Wait — but maybe color relates to the rectangle outline dims: outline 7x8 for rect1 (mixed) — interior parity safer. Actually maybe rule: fill with 7 if width and height of rectangle same parity? test rect1 7x8 mixed... risky. Interior parity: rect1 interior 5x5 odd→7. All consistent.

Submit.

The demo reveals the rule: fill each hollow rectangle's interior, using color 7 when the interior has odd dimensions and 2 when even (1x1→7, 2x2→2, 3x3→7, 3x5→7 all fit). Applying to the test: 9-rect (5x5 interior)→7, second 9-rect (6x6)→2, 5-rect (2x2)→2, 6-rect (3x3)→7.
